title: Vladivostok Air 352
summary: Vladivostok Air Flight 352, a Tupolev Tu-154M, crashed near Irkutsk on 4 July 2001 while approaching Irkutsk Airport. During approach, the first officer made erroneous control inputs including a nose-down input that disconnected the autopilot. The aircraft entered an excessive left bank of up to 48 degrees. Both pilots made alternating control inputs attempting recovery, and excessive nose-up input by both pilots induced an aerodynamic stall at insufficient altitude. The aircraft entered a corkscrew and crashed into farmland, killing all 145 aboard.
probable_cause: Russian investigation committee MAK attributed the causes to pilot error. During the approach, the crew made erroneous input on the aircraft's yoke, causing the airspeed to deplete. A series of errors caused the yoke to be excessively pulled, causing the aircraft to enter a corkscrew. The crew tried to recover but failed due to the aircraft's insufficient altitude.

factors.evidence: the first officer made erroneous nose down input of -4 degree and a left bank input into the steering column
the nose down input caused the autopilot to disconnect
the aircraft bank angle exceeded 48 degrees to the left, causing the aircraft to enter a corkscrew
the aircraft entered an aerodynamic stall due to excessive nose up input at high bank angle
the aircraft crashed into a farm field near Burdakovka, approximately 22 km from Irkutsk
the aircraft immediately exploded upon impact, killing all 145 people aboard

events.text: The flight took off from Yekaterinburg Koltsovo Airport at 19:47 local time and climbed to its cruising altitude of 10,000 m.
While the turn was being carried out by the crew, the bank angle suddenly increased and the first officer made a nose down input of -4 degree and a left bank input into the steering column.
A warning sounded as the first officer's input caused the autopilot to disconnect and the bank angle to increase from 20 degree to 30 degree.
Captain Goncharuk noticed the increasing bank angle and took over the control to correct the situation but the bank angle continued to increase up to 48 degrees.
The crew sensed an increase of the aircraft's vertical rate of descent and put an excessive nose up input into the yoke causing the aircraft to enter an aerodynamic stall at a severe left bank angle.
The aircraft crashed with its belly first near the settlement of Burdakovka, approximately 22 km from Irkutsk, and immediately exploded upon impact, instantly killing all 145 passengers and crew.

title: American Airlines 77
summary: American Airlines Flight 77 was hijacked by five al-Qaeda terrorists 31 minutes after taking off from Dulles on the morning of 11 September 2001. Lead hijacker Hani Hanjour, who had undergone extensive flight training, took control, disengaged the autopilot at 9:29 a.m. and flew a 330-degree spiral turn before deliberately crashing the Boeing 757 into the west side of the Pentagon at 09:37, killing all 64 aboard and 125 people in the building and igniting a large fire.
probable_cause: The aircraft was hijacked as part of the coordinated September 11 attacks and deliberately flown into the Pentagon by lead hijacker Hani Hanjour.

factors.evidence: hijacked by five al-Qaeda terrorists on the morning of September 11, 2001
Indianapolis Air Route Traffic Control was unaware of the hijackings of American Airlines Flight 11 and United Airlines Flight 175, Flight 77 was initially wrongly treated as a presumed plane crash
the terrorists aboard Flight 77 disengaged the autopilot and took manual control of the plane
caused a large fire that took several days to extinguish

events.text: Flight 77 became airborne from Dulles International Airport at 08:20 EDT.
Thirty-one minutes after takeoff, the hijackers stormed the cockpit and forced the passengers and crew to the rear of the cabin.

Because Indianapolis Air Route Traffic Control was unaware of the hijackings of Flight 11 and Flight 175, Flight 77 was initially wrongly treated as a presumed plane crash after it vanished from radar.
At 9:29 a.m., the hijackers aboard Flight 77 disengaged the autopilot and took manual control of the plane, turning and descending rapidly toward Washington.
Five miles west-southwest of the Pentagon, the aircraft made a 330-degree spiral turn clockwise, descending 2,200 feet by the end of the revolution.
Hanjour flew the aircraft into the west side of the Pentagon at 09:37, killing all 64 aboard and 125 people in the building, and igniting a large fire that took several days to extinguish.

title: American Airlines 11
summary: Boeing 767 was hijacked by five al-Qaeda terrorists as part of the September 11 attacks. Less than 15 minutes after takeoff, the hijackers attacked the flight crew. Flight attendants Karen Martin and Barbara Arestegui were stabbed and a passenger Daniel Lewin was killed. The hijackers breached the cockpit while forcing other passengers and crew to the rear of the aircraft. Lead hijacker Mohamed Atta assumed control and deliberately descended toward Manhattan. Three minutes before impact, Atta completed his final turn toward the World Trade Center.
probable_cause: Deliberate act by al-Qaeda hijackers who took control of the aircraft and deliberately crashed it into a building as part of coordinated suicide terrorist attacks.

title: United Airlines 175
summary: Five al-Qaeda hijackers led by Marwan al-Shehhi took control of Flight 175 after murdering the captain and first officer within 28 minutes of departure. Marwan al-Shehhi piloted the aircraft in a steep power dive at over 5000 ft per minute descent rate, impacting the South Tower at 09:59 EDT at approximately 587 mph, striking floors 77 through 85.
probable_cause: The aircraft was deliberately crashed into the South Tower by trained pilot hijacker al-Shehhi as part of the coordinated September 11 terrorist attacks.

title: Siberia Airlines 1812
summary: Siberia Airlines Flight 1812 was shot down over the Black Sea by an S-200 air defense missile fired by Ukrainian forces during joint Ukrainian-Russian military air-defense exercises at Cape Opuk in Crimea. The aircraft was cruising at 36,000 feet when Russian ground control lost contact. Ukrainian officials initially denied responsibility but later acknowledged that a Ukrainian S-200 missile had been launched seaward and locked onto the passenger aircraft instead of its intended target drone, with the missile detonating 15 meters above the aircraft, destroying it completely.
probable_cause: The aircraft was struck by an S-200 surface-to-air missile fired by Ukrainian armed forces during military training exercises. The missile, which had overshot its intended target drone and should have self-destructed, instead locked onto the passenger aircraft and detonated, destroying the aircraft and killing all 78 people on board.

title: 2001 Linate Airport runway collision
summary: During heavy fog with visibility less than 200 meters, a Cessna Citation business jet taxied along the wrong route and crossed an active runway where an MD-87 had just been cleared for takeoff. The aircraft collided at 150 knots, and the MD-87 departed the runway to strike a luggage hangar at 136 knots. All occupants of both aircraft and four ground personnel were killed. The investigation found the immediate cause was the Cessna's incursion but revealed systemic failures: no functional ground radar, obscured taxiway signs, deactivated motion-sensing alarms, and poor phraseology matching between ATC and airport signage.
probable_cause: The immediate cause was the incursion of the Cessna aircraft onto the active runway. However, the accident resulted from multiple systemic failures including the absence of a functioning ground radar system, obscured or worn taxiway signs, deactivated runway incursion alarms, and incompatible ATC terminology.

factors.evidence: The accident occurred in thick fog, with visibility reduced to less than 200 m
The Cessna pilot taxied along the southern taxi route (taxiway R6), crossing Runway 36R towards the main taxiway
Linate Airport was operating without a functioning ground radar system at the time, despite having had a new system approved on 30 March 1995
Guidance signs along the taxiways were obscured, or badly worn, and were later found not to meet regulations
The ground controller's verbal directions used terminology to designate aprons, taxiways, and runways, which did not match their on-the-ground signage and labels
Motion sensing runway incursion alarms were present, but had been deactivated to prevent false alarms from ground vehicles or animals
At 08:09:28, the MD-87 was given clearance to take off from Runway 36R, and fifty-three seconds later, the aircraft collided with the Cessna
The crash and subsequent fire killed all occupants of the MD-87, with 54 of them suffering severe burns

events.text: The Cessna was instructed to taxi from the western apron along the northern taxiway R5 to avoid Runway 36R
The Cessna pilot taxied along the southern taxi route (taxiway R6), crossing Runway 36R in thick fog with visibility less than 200 m
The Cessna reported its position at taxiway stop-marking S4, which was not on the controller's maps and was unknown to him
The MD-87 was given clearance by a different controller to take off from Runway 36R
The MD-87 aircraft, travelling at about 150 knots, collided with the Cessna on the runway
The aircraft left the runway and collided with a luggage hangar near the runway's end at approximately 136 knots

title: American Airlines 587
summary: American Airlines Flight 587, an Airbus A300 bound for Santo Domingo, crashed into Belle Harbor, Queens shortly after taking off from JFK on November 12, 2001, killing 265. The NTSB found First Officer Molin's aggressive alternating rudder inputs during wake turbulence from a preceding Japan Airlines 747 overstressed the vertical stabilizer until it separated, causing a flat spin and loss of control; both engines then sheared off.
probable_cause: The NTSB cited the first officer's unnecessary, excessive rudder inputs in response to wake turbulence, which exceeded the vertical stabilizer's design loads and caused it to separate, leading to loss of control.

factors.evidence: Molin moved the rudder right to left and back in quick succession, causing sideslip that broke the stabilizer.
The rudder use resulted from a flawed training scenario that exaggerated wake turbulence effects.
The composite lugs attaching the vertical stabilizer failed and it separated, falling into Jamaica Bay.
The aircraft pitched downward, entered a flat spin, and the loads sheared both engines off.

events.text: At 9:13:28 the A300 was cleared for takeoff about a minute 40 seconds behind a departing Japan Airlines 747.
The FDR showed the aircraft encountering wake turbulence from the JAL 747 ahead at 9:15:36.
Molin moved the rudder right to left and back in quick succession from 9:15:52, generating sideslip.
The vertical stabilizer's composite lugs failed at 9:15:58 and it separated, falling into Jamaica Bay.
The aircraft pitched downward into a flat spin and aerodynamic loads sheared both engines off, cutting FDR power at 9:16:01.
Molin said "What the hell are we into, we're stuck in it," and States replied "Get out of it, get out of it."

notes: Terrorism was initially suspected but ruled out; cause was rudder overuse and a flawed training scenario
